title: Paul's defense before Agrippa: his conversion retold + “almost thou persuadest me”

paragraphs.text: And Agrippa said unto Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretched forth his hand, and made his defence:
paragraphs.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον ἔφη· Ἐπιτρέπεταί σοι ὑπὲρ σεαυτοῦ λέγειν. τότε ὁ Παῦλος ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἀπελογεῖτο·
paragraphs.translit: Agrippas de pros ton Paulon ephē· Epitrepetai soi hyper seautou legein. tote ho Paulos ekteinas tēn cheira apelogeito·

paragraphs.text: I think myself happy, king Agrippa, that I am to make my defense before thee this day touching all the things whereof I am accused by the Jews:
paragraphs.original: Περὶ πάντων ὧν ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, ἥγημαι ἐμαυτὸν μακάριον ἐπὶ σοῦ μέλλων σήμερον ἀπολογεῖσθαι,
paragraphs.translit: Peri pantōn hōn enkaloumai hypo Ioudaiōn, basileu Agrippa, hēgēmai emauton makarion epi sou mellōn sēmeron apologeisthai,

paragraphs.text: especially because thou art expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
paragraphs.original: μάλιστα γνώστην ὄντα σε πάντων τῶν κατὰ Ἰουδαίους ἐθῶν τε καὶ ζητημάτων· διὸ δέομαι μακροθύμως ἀκοῦσαί μου.
paragraphs.translit: malista gnōstēn onta se pantōn tōn kata Ioudaious ethōn te kai zētēmatōn· dio deomai makrothymōs akousai mou.

paragraphs.text: My manner of life then from my youth up, which was from the beginning among mine own nation and at Jerusalem, know all the Jews;
paragraphs.original: Τὴν μὲν οὖν βίωσίν μου τὴν ἐκ νεότητος τὴν ἀπʼ ἀρχῆς γενομένην ἐν τῷ ἔθνει μου ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις ἴσασι πάντες Ἰουδαῖοι,
paragraphs.translit: Tēn men oun biōsin mou tēn ek neotētos tēn apʼ archēs genomenēn en tō ethnei mou en te Hierosolymois isasi pantes Ioudaioi,

paragraphs.text: having knowledge of me from the first, if they be willing to testify, that after the straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
paragraphs.original: προγινώσκοντές με ἄνωθεν, ἐὰν θέλωσι μαρτυρεῖν, ὅτι κατὰ τὴν ἀκριβεστάτην αἵρεσιν τῆς ἡμετέρας θρησκείας ἔζησα Φαρισαῖος.
paragraphs.translit: proginōskontes me anōthen, ean thelōsi martyrein, hoti kata tēn akribestatēn hairesin tēs hēmeteras thrēskeias ezēsa Pharisaios.

paragraphs.text: And now I stand [here] to be judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers;
paragraphs.original: καὶ νῦν ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι τῆς εἰς τοὺς πατέρας ἡμῶν ἐπαγγελίας γενομένης ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἕστηκα κρινόμενος,
paragraphs.translit: kai nyn epʼ elpidi tēs eis tous pateras hēmōn epangelias genomenēs hypo tou theou hestēka krinomenos,

paragraphs.text: unto which [promise] our twelve tribes, earnestly serving [God] night and day, hope to attain. And concerning this hope I am accused by the Jews, O king!
paragraphs.original: εἰς ἣν τὸ δωδεκάφυλον ἡμῶν ἐν ἐκτενείᾳ νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν λατρεῦον ἐλπίζει καταντῆσαι· περὶ ἧς ἐλπίδος ἐγκαλοῦμαι ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων, βασιλεῦ·
paragraphs.translit: eis hēn to dōdekaphylon hēmōn en ekteneia nykta kai hēmeran latreuon elpizei katantēsai· peri hēs elpidos enkaloumai hypo Ioudaiōn, basileu·

paragraphs.text: Why is it judged incredible with you, if God doth raise the dead?
paragraphs.original: τί ἄπιστον κρίνεται παρʼ ὑμῖν εἰ ὁ θεὸς νεκροὺς ἐγείρει;
paragraphs.translit: ti apiston krinetai parʼ hymin ei ho theos nekrous egeirei;

paragraphs.text: I verily thought with myself that I ought to do many things contrary to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
paragraphs.original: Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ἔδοξα ἐμαυτῷ πρὸς τὸ ὄνομα Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου δεῖν πολλὰ ἐναντία πρᾶξαι·
paragraphs.translit: Egō men oun edoxa emautō pros to onoma Iēsou tou Nazōraiou dein polla enantia praxai·

paragraphs.text: And this I also did in Jerusalem: and I both shut up many of the saints in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were put to death I gave my vote against them.
paragraphs.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησα ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις, καὶ πολλούς τε τῶν ἁγίων ἐγὼ ἐν φυλακαῖς κατέκλεισα τὴν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων ἐξουσίαν λαβών, ἀναιρουμένων τε αὐτῶν κατήνεγκα ψῆφον,
paragraphs.translit: ho kai epoiēsa en Hierosolymois, kai pollous te tōn hagiōn egō en phylakais katekleisa tēn para tōn archiereōn exousian labōn, anairoumenōn te autōn katēnenka psēphon,

paragraphs.text: And punishing them oftentimes in all the synagogues, I strove to make them blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto foreign cities.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατὰ πάσας τὰς συναγωγὰς πολλάκις τιμωρῶν αὐτοὺς ἠνάγκαζον βλασφημεῖν, περισσῶς τε ἐμμαινόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐδίωκον ἕως καὶ εἰς τὰς ἔξω πόλεις.
paragraphs.translit: kai kata pasas tas synagōgas pollakis timōrōn autous ēnankazon blasphēmein, perissōs te emmainomenos autois ediōkon heōs kai eis tas exō poleis.

paragraphs.text: Whereupon as I journeyed to Damascus with the authority and commission of the chief priests,
paragraphs.original: Ἐν οἷς πορευόμενος εἰς τὴν Δαμασκὸν μετʼ ἐξουσίας καὶ ἐπιτροπῆς τῆς τῶν ἀρχιερέων
paragraphs.translit: En hois poreuomenos eis tēn Damaskon metʼ exousias kai epitropēs tēs tōn archiereōn

paragraphs.text: at midday, O king, I saw on the way a light from heaven, above the brightness of the sun, shining round about me and them that journeyed with me.
paragraphs.original: ἡμέρας μέσης κατὰ τὴν ὁδὸν εἶδον, βασιλεῦ, οὐρανόθεν ὑπὲρ τὴν λαμπρότητα τοῦ ἡλίου περιλάμψαν με φῶς καὶ τοὺς σὺν ἐμοὶ πορευομένους·
paragraphs.translit: hēmeras mesēs kata tēn hodon eidon, basileu, ouranothen hyper tēn lamprotēta tou hēliou perilampsan me phōs kai tous syn emoi poreuomenous·

paragraphs.text: And when we were all fallen to the earth, I heard a voice saying unto me in the Hebrew language, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? it is hard for thee to kick against the goad.
paragraphs.original: πάντων τε καταπεσόντων ἡμῶν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἤκουσα φωνὴν λέγουσαν πρός με τῇ Ἑβραΐδι διαλέκτῳ· Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις; σκληρόν σοι πρὸς κέντρα λακτίζειν.
paragraphs.translit: pantōn te katapesontōn hēmōn eis tēn gēn ēkousa phōnēn legousan pros me tē Hebraidi dialektō· Saoul Saoul, ti me diōkeis; sklēron soi pros kentra laktizein.

paragraphs.text: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest.
paragraphs.original: ἐγὼ δὲ εἶπα· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ δὲ κύριος εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·
paragraphs.translit: egō de eipa· Tis ei, kyrie; ho de kyrios eipen· Egō eimi Iēsous hon sy diōkeis·

paragraphs.text: But arise, and stand upon thy feet: for to this end have I appeared unto thee, to appoint thee a minister and a witness both of the things wherein thou hast seen me, and of the things wherein I will appear unto thee;
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ στῆθι ἐπὶ τοὺς πόδας σου· εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὤφθην σοι, προχειρίσασθαί σε ὑπηρέτην καὶ μάρτυρα ὧν τε εἶδές με ὧν τε ὀφθήσομαί σοι,
paragraphs.translit: alla anastēthi kai stēthi epi tous podas sou· eis touto gar ōphthēn soi, procheirisasthai se hypēretēn kai martyra hōn te eides me hōn te ophthēsomai soi,

paragraphs.text: delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom I send thee,
paragraphs.original: ἐξαιρούμενός σε ἐκ τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἐθνῶν, εἰς οὓς ἐγὼ ἀποστέλλω σε
paragraphs.translit: exairoumenos se ek tou laou kai ek tōn ethnōn, eis hous egō apostellō se

paragraphs.text: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive remission of sins and an inheritance among them that are sanctified by faith in me.
paragraphs.original: ἀνοῖξαι ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν, τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι ἀπὸ σκότους εἰς φῶς καὶ τῆς ἐξουσίας τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, τοῦ λαβεῖν αὐτοὺς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ κλῆρον ἐν τοῖς ἡγιασμένοις πίστει τῇ εἰς ἐμέ.
paragraphs.translit: anoixai ophthalmous autōn, tou epistrepsai apo skotous eis phōs kai tēs exousias tou Satana epi ton theon, tou labein autous aphesin hamartiōn kai klēron en tois hēgiasmenois pistei tē eis eme.

paragraphs.text: Wherefore, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient unto the heavenly vision:
paragraphs.original: Ὅθεν, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, οὐκ ἐγενόμην ἀπειθὴς τῇ οὐρανίῳ ὀπτασίᾳ,
paragraphs.translit: Hothen, basileu Agrippa, ouk egenomēn apeithēs tē ouraniō optasia,

paragraphs.text: but declared both to them of Damascus first and at Jerusalem, and throughout all the country of Judaea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.
paragraphs.original: ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐν Δαμασκῷ πρῶτόν τε καὶ Ἱεροσολύμοις, πᾶσάν τε τὴν χώραν τῆς Ἰουδαίας, καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἀπήγγελλον μετανοεῖν καὶ ἐπιστρέφειν ἐπὶ τὸν θεόν, ἄξια τῆς μετανοίας ἔργα πράσσοντας.
paragraphs.translit: alla tois en Damaskō prōton te kai Hierosolymois, pasan te tēn chōran tēs Ioudaias, kai tois ethnesin apēngellon metanoein kai epistrephein epi ton theon, axia tēs metanoias erga prassontas.

paragraphs.text: For this cause the Jews seized me in the temple, and assayed to kill me.
paragraphs.original: ἕνεκα τούτων με Ἰουδαῖοι συλλαβόμενοι ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ἐπειρῶντο διαχειρίσασθαι.
paragraphs.translit: heneka toutōn me Ioudaioi syllabomenoi en tō hierō epeirōnto diacheirisasthai.

paragraphs.text: Having therefore obtained the help that is from God, I stand unto this day testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets and Moses did say should come;
paragraphs.original: ἐπικουρίας οὖν τυχὼν τῆς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης ἕστηκα μαρτυρόμενος μικρῷ τε καὶ μεγάλῳ, οὐδὲν ἐκτὸς λέγων ὧν τε οἱ προφῆται ἐλάλησαν μελλόντων γίνεσθαι καὶ Μωϋσῆς,
paragraphs.translit: epikourias oun tychōn tēs apo tou theou achri tēs hēmeras tautēs hestēka martyromenos mikrō te kai megalō, ouden ektos legōn hōn te hoi prophētai elalēsan mellontōn ginesthai kai Mōysēs,

paragraphs.text: how that the Christ must suffer, [and] how that he first by the resurrection of the dead should proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles.
paragraphs.original: εἰ παθητὸς ὁ χριστός, εἰ πρῶτος ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν φῶς μέλλει καταγγέλλειν τῷ τε λαῷ καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ei pathētos ho christos, ei prōtos ex anastaseōs nekrōn phōs mellei katangellein tō te laō kai tois ethnesin.

paragraphs.text: And as he thus made his defense, Festus saith with a loud voice, Paul, thou art mad; thy much learning is turning thee mad.
paragraphs.original: Ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἀπολογουμένου ὁ Φῆστος μεγάλῃ τῇ φωνῇ φησιν· Μαίνῃ, Παῦλε· τὰ πολλά σε γράμματα εἰς μανίαν περιτρέπει.
paragraphs.translit: Tauta de autou apologoumenou ho Phēstos megalē tē phōnē phēsin· Mainē, Paule· ta polla se grammata eis manian peritrepei.

paragraphs.text: But Paul saith, I am not mad, most excellent Festus; but speak forth words of truth and soberness.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος· Οὐ μαίνομαι, φησίν, κράτιστε Φῆστε, ἀλλὰ ἀληθείας καὶ σωφροσύνης ῥήματα ἀποφθέγγομαι.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Paulos· Ou mainomai, phēsin, kratiste Phēste, alla alētheias kai sōphrosynēs rhēmata apophthengomai.

paragraphs.text: For the king knoweth of these things, unto whom also I speak freely: for I am persuaded that none of these things is hidden from him; for this hath not been done in a corner.
paragraphs.original: ἐπίσταται γὰρ περὶ τούτων ὁ βασιλεύς, πρὸς ὃν καὶ παρρησιαζόμενος λαλῶ· λανθάνειν γὰρ αὐτὸν τούτων οὐ πείθομαι οὐθέν, οὐ γάρ ἐστιν ἐν γωνίᾳ πεπραγμένον τοῦτο.
paragraphs.translit: epistatai gar peri toutōn ho basileus, pros hon kai parrēsiazomenos lalō· lanthanein gar auton toutōn ou peithomai outhen, ou gar estin en gōnia pepragmenon touto.

paragraphs.text: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.
paragraphs.original: πιστεύεις, βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα, τοῖς προφήταις; οἶδα ὅτι πιστεύεις.
paragraphs.translit: pisteueis, basileu Agrippa, tois prophētais; oida hoti pisteueis.

paragraphs.text: And Agrippa [said] unto Paul, With but little persuasion thou wouldest fain make me a Christian.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἀγρίππας πρὸς τὸν Παῦλον· Ἐν ὀλίγῳ με πείθεις Χριστιανὸν ποιῆσαι.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Agrippas pros ton Paulon· En oligō me peitheis Christianon poiēsai.

paragraphs.text: And Paul [said], I would to God, that whether with little or with much, not thou only, but also all that hear me this day, might become such as I am, except these bonds.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Παῦλος· Εὐξαίμην ἂν τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐν ὀλίγῳ καὶ ἐν μεγάλῳ οὐ μόνον σὲ ἀλλὰ καὶ πάντας τοὺς ἀκούοντάς μου σήμερον γενέσθαι τοιούτους ὁποῖος καὶ ἐγώ εἰμι παρεκτὸς τῶν δεσμῶν τούτων.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Paulos· Euxaimēn an tō theō kai en oligō kai en megalō ou monon se alla kai pantas tous akouontas mou sēmeron genesthai toioutous hopoios kai egō eimi parektos tōn desmōn toutōn.

paragraphs.text: And the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice, and they that sat with them:
paragraphs.original: Ἀνέστη τε ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἥ τε Βερνίκη καὶ οἱ συγκαθήμενοι αὐτοῖς,
paragraphs.translit: Anestē te ho basileus kai ho hēgemōn hē te Bernikē kai hoi synkathēmenoi autois,

paragraphs.text: and when they had withdrawn, they spake one to another, saying, This man doeth nothing worthy of death or of bonds.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναχωρήσαντες ἐλάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες ὅτι Οὐδὲν θανάτου ἢ δεσμῶν ἄξιον τι πράσσει ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος.
paragraphs.translit: kai anachōrēsantes elaloun pros allēlous legontes hoti Ouden thanatou ē desmōn axion ti prassei ho anthrōpos houtos.

paragraphs.text: And Agrippa said unto Festus, This man might have been set at liberty, if he had not appealed unto Caesar.
paragraphs.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ τῷ Φήστῳ ἔφη· Ἀπολελύσθαι ἐδύνατο ὁ ἄνθρωπος οὗτος εἰ μὴ ἐπεκέκλητο Καίσαρα.
paragraphs.translit: Agrippas de tō Phēstō ephē· Apolelysthai edynato ho anthrōpos houtos ei mē epekeklēto Kaisara.
